analysis.title: US Capital Markets Perspectives, October 2026
key_insights: Federated Hermes projects 2026 global GDP growth of 3%. US Q2 2026 GDP grew 2.2% annualized. The report names AI-related business investment, manufacturing and consumer spending as the main drivers of earnings and growth.
Inflation is described as sticky and above the Fed's 2% target. The report cites high energy, freight and food costs as the sources.
The Fed raised rates by 0.25% on September 16, 2026. The report says FOMC members and markets expect further hikes. Inflation has overtaken the labor market as the immediate policy concern.
The September US jobs report was weaker than expected. Unemployment was 4.2% in September, which the report still calls a relatively strong labor market.
AI capex has supported equity markets. Hyperscalers are issuing record levels of debt in 2026, which competes with the Treasury market for buyers.
The 10-year Treasury yield has risen 132 basis points since the start of the Iran war and reached 5.29% on 9/30/26. The 10-year term premium has also risen.
Real yields are rising because of resilient growth, heavy AI infrastructure capex and heavy government debt supply, which the report calls a structural repricing of rates.
Oil rose above $100 per barrel after the Iran war began and has moved above and below that level since. The ECB, BOJ and Fed have begun raising rates, while the BoE held.
In Q1 2026 AI-related investment contributed 1.34 points to US GDP growth of 2%. The report says the AI boom is still climbing after year three, while earlier booms peaked at year three.

The report says disinflation requires lower energy prices. It names policy error as a risk if the Fed hikes by more than markets expect, especially if growth weakens under higher mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment.

Federated Hermes advises diversification beyond top-tier tech into international and emerging markets, US small caps and alternatives. It cites inflation, volatility, geopolitical risk and possible fiscal policy changes after the US mid-term elections.

The report lays out four scenarios: resilient growth with slow disinflation, inflation persistence (stagflation lite), productivity-led growth, and a downside shock or hard landing, which it calls a tail risk.

sector_views.rationale: The report lists dividend stocks and value equity as holdings that have shown potential to add to performance in the inflation persistence scenario.
The report lists large, mid and small-cap growth as holdings that have shown potential to add to performance in the productivity-led growth scenario.

earnings_insights: Federated Hermes forecasts S&P 500 EPS of $370 for 2026 and $425 for 2027 (forecast, as of 10/15/26). Its target forward P/E is 20.0x for 2026 and 20.4x for 2027.
The report says strong earnings, led by AI-related business investment, manufacturing and consumer spending, are key economic drivers.

tension_points.bull_case: The report describes resilient growth with slow disinflation. Much of the expected tightening is already priced in. In the productivity-led scenario, falling core inflation lets the Fed ease without a recession.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed hikes more than markets expect while growth weakens under higher mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment, which makes policy error a risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy prices need to fall for disinflation to begin. The report says the downside shock scenario would come from a shock that appears or accelerates rapidly.
